newsitem.title: UK: S&P gives Sweden's Akademiska Hus MTN an AA rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P gives Sweden's Akademiska Hus MTN an AA rating.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Friday it assigned its AA senior unsecured rating to the five billion crown medium term note program of Statliga Akademiska Hus AB (Akademiska Hus).
In a related action, S&P said it assigned Akademiska Hus its AA long-term and A1 plus short-term issuer credit rating.

"The ratings reflect the government ownership, the Swedish state's strong involvement in the higher education sector, Akademiska Hus' domination on the university premises market in Sweden, and the stable customer base," S&P said in a statement. There are no intentions of ownership changes, S&P said.
The company was formed in October 1993, and manages 2.3 billion square meters of university premises to a total book value of around 15 billion crowns (US$2.3 billion).
Akademiska Hus has a stable cash flow and earnings with pretax funds from operations interest coverage of 3.3 times and pretax net interest coverage of 2.5 times in 1995, S&P said.
Net income after interest and tax was 400 million crowns. Equity to assets ratio is around 37 percent and debt to total capital ratio 63 percent.

While income and operating costs should be fairly predictable, interest costs may fluctuate. Based on an estimated net debt of 9.5 billion crowns, a one percent change of interest affects the profit by 95 million crowns, S&P said.
S&P said the outlook was stable.

Akademiska Hus' operations and cash flows are stable, and the Swedish government presently have no plans of any major changes of the universities' regulatory and financial framework. However, Standard & Poor's will monitor the future development of the higher education sector, as well as Akademiska Hus.
